  "text": "By morning, the harbor drawing had dried flat beneath a stack of hymnals. Mara carried it to the quay, where Daniel and Mr. Venn were waiting beside a borrowed skiff. Mrs. Bell stood with them, her boots already muddy.

“She knows the outer wall,” Mr. Venn said.

Mrs. Bell took the drawing and studied the seven pencil marks. “Your father showed me six,” she said. “Not this one.”

They rowed past the church as the tide fell. At each mark, Daniel held the skiff steady while Mara searched the stones. Most were easy to find: a notch, a rusted ring, a circle crossed by a stroke. At the fifth, Mrs. Bell reached into a crack and drew out a strip of blue cloth, stiff with salt.

“That wasn’t there last spring,” she said.

Near the outermost mark, the water grew shallow enough to show the seabed. Mara saw a line of pale stones running away from the wall toward the channel. They did not appear on their father’s drawing.

Daniel leaned over the gunwale. “Is that a path?”

Mrs. Bell shook her head. “It’s the top of something buried.”

A knock sounded beneath the skiff. Daniel lifted his oar, but the sound came again, three measured taps. Mara looked toward the church steps. The tide had uncovered the iron staple there.

Mr. Venn set a finger on the seventh mark in the notebook. “We’ll need a longer rope,” he said.

Mara added it to the list. Then she drew the line of pale stones before the water could hide them again."
